body:
Followup to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41045

- "obj" refers to structured (non-scalar `Object`) option values.
- "optval" generally refers to the internal scalar (legacy ":set"-style) option value.

Related:

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/25672

comment_data.body: I'm pretty confused too. The function is called `optval_to_varp`, but the variable is an `Object`, and it's still called `optval_right`, not `varp_right`. Several of the other `varp` named functions deal with `Object`, which seems backwards from the PR description.

`Object` may be used for representing the legacy "varp" value too, depending on various functions. 

That's not new, but yes it's confusing. I will think about this.

(Note: they are distinguishable because complex (non-scalar) varp `Object` have string type, whereas complex structured `Object` only have array/dict type.)

That's really confusing... I would expect "varp" to refer to a pointer to an option variable, not an option value. What's wrong with calling a structured `Object` "object", and calling a varp `Object` "optval"?

comment_regular_data.body: I cannot understand the changes in this PR.

Are you confused by `varp`, `optval`, or both?

After my recent options refactors, we now have 2 ways to represent an option value instead of 3. 

The two option value forms are:

1. Legacy ":set"-style (what is stored in `p_foo` globals).
2. Structured (`Object`).

We need names for those things. I chose `varp` (because we already have 4+ functions using that name) and `optval`. If you have a different suggestion lmk.

Alternative idea: avoid "varp" in most function names, and just assume that `opt_` or `option_` functions work with "varp" (unless they mention `optval_`). So instead of `opt_varp_free`, name it `opt_free`. WDYT?
An alternative is optval and optp (because pointer to option is more specific than pointer to variable).
I looked at the code and I don't see any inconsistency in the current naming.

appreciate the feedback. i'll revert most of this and orient more towards:

> What's wrong with calling a structured `Object` "object", and calling a varp `Object` "optval"?
updated patch + PR desc. I agree this is better, thanks for pushback.
